Explanation about the recently released videos that include the confession on setting fire to the paddy rice straws from Kanda Muslim Village, Po Khaung Chaung Village Tract, Buthedaung Township
 
 June 30, 2022
 
 There was a case of setting fire on purpose to the paddy rice straws of Morjubi and Mamauk from Kanda Muslim Village, Po Khaung Chaung Village Tract, Buthedaung Township, State of Arakan at 7:45 PM, December 21, 2021. The Arakan People's Authority had been able to find out the true culprits timely after investigating the case.
 
 Despite knowing the real nature of the case after the investigation, our government did not disclose the evidence and kept it confidential at that time because we were concerned that it could lead to the ethnic and religious tensions under the exaggeration and manipulation of some people and organizations and wanted a small issue not to be a bigger one. We, therefore, just arrested and imprisoned some perpetrators in line with the existing law.
 
 The repetitive questionnaires towards our organization about this case confessed by the culprits in the videos have been reported these days. Besides, since there are partial and dishonest accusations against our organization and endeavors to mobilize the people for bad purposes and efforts to cover the crimes of real culprits by blaming others on this case, our organization has now decided to release timely these confidential pieces of evidence so that the public knows about the real contexts of the case.
 
 As there were some instances attempting to cover the truths and destroy the evidences behind the cases and events that happened in Arakan while misusing Human Rights politics by some groups of people, our organization has already sent the records, reports, and pieces of evidence about this case to the International Organizations, Embassies, and other suitable actors since the January of this year, 2022.
 
 After investigating this case thoroughly, it is evidently found that some people who are working with the international organizations for the sake of Human Rights are also deliberately pouring gasoline on the fire while systematically creating ethnic and religious conflict and instability in the region.
 
 Therefore, our organization must disclose this case unavoidably due to a situation in which some groups of people using the International Organizations under the banner of Human Rights are now consistently trying to destabilize peace and order in the region intentionally.

Battle Report

September 18, 2022

The Myanmar Army has been conducting a joint ground and air offensive against the Arakan Army (ARA) in three locations, south and northeast of Nhamada village in Paletwa Township and northwest of Thathi Kone village, for almost a month.

The Arakan Army has cut off and surrounded some of the Myanmar Army’s military bases and movement lines in the Paletwa region of Rakhine State, and the Myanmar Army is making special efforts to open the supply, support, and transportation routes of their military bases and movement lines. Therefore, despite the fact that the Arakan Army is making strenuous efforts to prevent the blockade of their military bases and movement lines with air and artillery support almost every day, the Arakan Army continues to block the enemy.

The Arakan Army finally captured the enemy's camp near Milepost (40) on the Rakhine-Bengal border on August 31, 2022, after a month of blockade and siege. On September 10, 2022, it captured another camp of the 352nd Infantry Battalion. In addition, the enemy's Thandaung strategic camp was also blocked for more than three months, and the Arakan Army has now captured the Thandaung strategic camp. The enemy has already abandoned many of their camps on the border.

We are also blocking some other enemy camps in the same way. Among them is the "Myeikwa camp" near the India-Bangladesh-Myanmar tri-border.

At the same time, Paletwa Township, The Myanmar military has been attacking our troops about (2) kilometers south of Nhamada village for almost a month now, with fighting continuing daily in the surrounding area.

On September (18), 2022, from (1) 48:00 PM, the enemy launched three (3) fighter jets and two (2) helicopter gunships at our troops about (2) kilometers south of Nhamada village, alternating until (3) 3:00 PM. During today’s airstrike, three (3) fighter jets fired bombs and rockets (11) times, the most consecutive attacks of about (30) minutes without stopping. Then, two (2) helicopter gunships attacked the area for more than half an hour. The enemy’s artillery and ground-based artillery also continued to fire at the area. Therefore, our side fired back with heavy weapons at the Mee Wa strategic position.

The enemy has launched ground attacks on the area with heavy weapons and air support (7) times, but the Arakan Army soldiers continue to withstand the enemy's attacks with great courage, strong fighting spirit, obedience to orders, and good courage.

We would like to pay tribute to the Arakan soldiers who are fighting bravely and with great obedience to orders.

 Call for humanitarian assistance for an emergency response
  to Cyclone Mocha in Arakan
 
 On May 14, 2023, Cyclone Mocha passed through the Arakan Coast, with landfall on Sittwe and sweeping through most of the townships and villages across Rakhine, leaving a trail of devastation along its path. Mocha is a highly severe cyclone with wind gusts of 100-120 miles per hour. And it did destroy many basic infrastructures in Arakan, such as houses, religious buildings, schools, hospitals, power grids, communication towers, riverside roads and sidewalks. And it was reported that there were some cases of casualties and injuries caused by Cyclone Mocha.
 
 Currently, the people affected by Cyclone Mocha are facing severe difficulties, such as no shelter and lack of food and medicine, and the public has no further assistance and emergency aid due to the interruption of communication networks (mobile phones, internet) and transportation.
 
 The United League of Arakan calls for immediate help and assistance from the leading countries, the ASEAN countries and other international actors for urgently delivering immediate relief and necessities, such as shelter, food, medicine and other basic needs to the affected communities.
 
 And we are deeply grateful to the civil society organizations, charity groups, and the good-willing public, which were actively cooperating with us during the evacuation process before the storm.

Statement 
 
 July 14, 2023
 
 
 Today is the day which has been two months since Cyclone Mocha has struck. On May 14, 2023, ULA formed Cyclone Mocha ERRCA committee with the aim of carrying out emergency and rescue activities in the townships across Rakhine where the cyclone has passed as its center and devastated mostly. By utilizing the human resources and financial ones both from our political, administrative, civilian and military departments of the organization, and from the domestic and international communities, we are able to manage and perform the relief work successfully.
 
 Therefore, two months after the cyclone, more than 75 percent of the affected population is now re-sheltered and we are also in consistent efforts to shelter the rest as fast as possible. For our part, we are trying our best to restore the broken transportation, provide rice seeds and help farmers plant seasonal fruits, deliver health services, and support the basic foods, clothes and shelters for the urgent and disaster-affected people. In addition, conducting survey projects is on the way to get more concrete data about the damage and loss of the cyclone which in turn can help our relief and rehabilitation activities.
 
 The Cyclone Mocha ERRCA committee would like to deeply recognize and thank all those people and individuals who have helped the Mocha cyclone-affected people of Arakkha morally, physically and financially. At the same time, since there are still many emergency needs and rehabilitation activities to be completed, we would like to request further humanitarian assistance and cooperation in every possible way. In addition, the ERRCA would like to urge the businesspersons, traders, and shopkeepers of construction materials not to sell home-construction items, rice, oil and salt and other basic commodities and medicines at unreasonable prices but to do so at a fair price.

Battle News Release 

January 14, 2024

As the saying goes, "Rome was not built in a day", none of the strategic positions, barracks, and artillery positions captured by the Arakan Army in the Rakhine and Paletwa regions were easily captured.

These positions were captured through the worthy sacrifices of the Arakan soldiers, the bravery of the soldiers who sacrificed themselves, the fulfillment of the orders and duties given, the ability to fight in conjunction with each other in the war zones, and the ability to seize the enemy's weaknesses. On the other hand, through connected battles and balanced battles, the enemy's positions were strategically captured one after another.

The important cities in northern Rakhine were attacked by the enemy's air, sea, Despite heavy artillery fire, our Rakhine Army was able to capture the important and key strategic hills, emplacements and artillery emplacements of the Military Council, which have been causing trouble to the people for many years, through fierce offensive attacks.

The operation in Paletwa began on November 13, 2023, and both “Tarong Ai” and “Non Bu” strategic areas were attacked in succession. Even before this offensive began, we had been strategically surrounding and blocking many strategic hills and emplacements of the Military Council in Rakhine and Paletwa for many years, and we are now attacking and destroying these areas one by one. 

Therefore, the military council’s strategic areas, namely Tarong Ai strategic area, Non Bu strategic area, Khwe strategic area, Point (377) strategic area, Shin Lethwa strategic area, The KLA (289) Battalion Headquarters, the SKA (19) Forward Division Headquarters, and the Miwa Strategic Hill were strategically and systematically captured one by one. Only after such capture was the entire city of Paletwa finally captured and successfully controlled.

Around Paletwa, the “KLA (289) Battalion Headquarters”, “SKA (19) Forward Division Headquarters” and “Division (11)” subordinate battalions are deployed east, west, south, and north centered on Paletwa.

“KLA (289) Battalion Headquarters” is a major divisional headquarters that manages and commands all their battalions in the entire Paletwa region, and is also the “military strategic hill” where division commanders jointly supervise.

All the battalions in Paletwa and the commanders of the “Saka Kha (19)” and “Division (11)” operating in Paletwa are located in Paletwa and are under command from there, making Paletwa the largest strategic base. 

The Arakan Army finally captured the “289th Battalion Headquarters” of the Military Council based in Paletwa at 7:10 a.m. on January 10, 2024. A large amount of enemy weapons and ammunition and military equipment were seized. 

This “289th Battalion Headquarters” is the last remaining camp to be captured among the many camps that they have surrounded in Paletwa. In addition, this battalion headquarters is the headquarters that manages and directs the military council’s operations in the entire Paletwa region, as well as the strategic support base that provides support to their military bases in the entire Paletwa region and the India-Bangladesh-Myanmar (Paletwa) tri-border. 

The last two remaining “Namada Strategy” and “Khankha Taung Strategy” camps of the military council in the Paletwa region, “Khankha Taung Strategy” camp, were also completely captured on January 13, 2024, and a large amount of ammunition was also seized. 🔳 What is a Tokamak?

Tokamaks (🔊-tokamak), also known as artificial suns, are electromagnetic nuclear fusion reactors, a Russian term. The reactor consists of a doughnut-shaped tunnel lined with magnets, and inside this tunnel, atoms such as deuterium and tritium are placed and heated with microwaves, causing the atoms to become a hot gas. The atoms used here are ions with fewer electrons than normal, so this gas also carries electricity. 

There are mainly four states of matter: solid, In addition to liquids and gases, electrically charged gases are also called "plasmas." These electrically charged gases are heated and made to move by nearby magnets. As they rotate, the gas expands further, and this expansion is controlled by the magnets, preventing it from exploding outwards. This "magnetized gas" is no longer allowed to expand as much as it wants, and eventually the magnetic repulsion between the atoms is overcome, causing extremely intense compression between the atoms, and the atoms collapse into their original form. 

As the original pairs of atoms break apart and transform into larger atoms, a small amount of the mass of the atoms is also lost. From this small amount of mass that is reduced or eliminated, energy is released as heat and light, which is the result of multiplying the mass by the speed of light squared. This is the release of a large amount of energy from a small amount of mass according to Einstein's law of mass-energy equivalence, known as E = mc², and this is called nuclear fusion. 

🔳 How can the resulting energy be used?

As mentioned above, during the continuous nuclear reactions in the Tokamak reactor, a large amount of heat energy is released, and as mentioned at the beginning, it reaches a temperature that is up to 8 times hotter than the core of the sun. Administrative capital Naypyidaw About Nay Pyi Taw
Nay Pyi Taw is the capital of Myanmar, located in the Nay Pyi Taw Union Territory. On 6 November 2005, the administrative capital of Myanmar was officially moved to a green field 2 miles (3.2 km) west of Pyinmana. It is approximately 200 miles (320 km) north of the former capital Yangon.
The city's official name was announced on Myanmar Armed Forces Day on 27 March 2006. As of 2009, it had a population of 925,000, making it the third most populous city in the country after Yangon and Mandalay. Much of the city is occupied by government buildings.
The Union Parliament, the Supreme Court, the Presidential Palace, and the Union Cabinet are located in Nay Pyi Taw. Nay Pyi Taw hosted the 24th and 25th ASEAN Summits, the 3rd BIMSTEC Summit, the 9th East Asia Summit, and the 2013 Southeast Asian Games.
Etymology
Nay Pyi Taw is generally translated as "royal capital", "royal palace" or "royal residence". Traditionally, it is used as a suffix for the capital cities. For example, Mandalay was called Yadanabon Naypyidaw.
History
Although the history of Nay Pyi Taw since its creation is relatively short, the current site where the capital is located is a very long one, as it was the headquarters of the Burma Independence Army (BIA) led by General Aung San, the father of Myanmar's independence. General Aung San marched from Thailand and established his headquarters at Pyinmana-Lewe. Therefore, the current capital of Nay Pyi Taw is located in the "Aung Myay" of Burma, where the Burmese independence movement began. Nay Pyi Taw was founded 2 miles (3.2 km) west of Pyinmana. Construction began approximately 200 miles (320 km) north of Yangon. The military government hired at least 25 construction companies, including Asia World and Htoo Limited, to carry out the construction work. Although not all construction work was completed, on November 6, 2005, the government began moving in groups to Nay Pyi Taw.
Five days later, at 11:00 a.m. on November 11, a second convoy of 1,100 military trucks left Yangon carrying 11 government ministries. All ministries were expected to be in place by the end of February 2006. However, the rapid relocation left schools and other facilities incomplete, and separated government employees from their families for a period of time. The government initially prevented families of government employees from moving to Nay Pyi Taw. Military headquarters were located in separate areas from government ministries. Civilians were barred from entering military and government facilities. Vendors are prohibited from entering the commercial zone near government offices. Officials use the abbreviation “Napata” for government work.
On March 27, 2006, more than 12,000 soldiers marched in the new capital in its first public demonstration. The parade was a large military parade to commemorate Tatmadaw Day, the anniversary of the uprising against Japanese occupation in 1945. Filming, video, and photography are prohibited inside the concrete parade ground, which houses three large statues of Burmese kings: Anawrahta, Bayinnaung, and Alaungpaya. The three kings are considered the most important kings in Burmese history. The city was officially named during the parade. The city’s official name was announced on Myanmar Armed Forces Day on March 27, 2006.

It is located in Lewe on the Yangon-Mandalay highway.
International Zone
The government has allocated two hectares of land for foreign embassies and UN missions.
Shopping
Central Junction Mall Nay Pyi Taw Myoma Market is currently the commercial hub of Nay Pyi Taw. Other shopping areas include Thapyay Kone Market and Central Junction Mall. Central Junction Mall was built by Shwe Taung Development Company and was the first privately owned market mall in Nay Pyi Taw, opening in August 2009. Myoma Market has a few restaurants and street food stalls, and there are also restaurants near Thapyay Kone Market. A few miles away, there are also restaurants in Lewe and Pyinmana where you can enjoy a delicious dinner.
Places of interest
Ngalay Lake Park is a small water park, located near Kwee Shin village, next to the Ngalay Dam (approximately seven miles from Nay Pyi Taw). Opened in 2008, Ngalay Lake Park features a water slide, nature trails, a pavilion, and a beach. The park is open to the public during Thingyan holidays.
Nay Pyi Taw Zoo opened in 2008 with 420 animals and a climate-controlled penguin enclosure. It is the largest zoo in Myanmar. Nay Pyi Taw Zoo is located 18 miles from Pyinmana, between Pyinmana and Tatkon. It covers an area of ​​612 acres and was established on 18 September 2007 and opened on 26 March 2008. Following the death of Queen Elizabeth, people in Africa and India have been demanding the return of some of her crown jewels.

Her remaining jewels, including the crown, are among the world's rarest and most expensive gems, which were seized by British colonies and whose ownership is disputed with their original countries.

Two of the most prominent gems being sought are the Koh-i-noor diamond from India and the Great Star of Africa, each estimated to be worth $400 million.

The Koh-i-noor diamond, weighing 105.6 carats, was mined in southern India in the early 1300s and was set into the crown jewels made for Elizabeth's mother, Elizabeth Angela Margaret Boisley, in 1937.

Mughal emperors, Iranian kings, Afghan kings and Sikh maharajas have claimed ownership of the diamond, claiming it to be the original owner. The diamond was acquired by the East India Company in 1849 from the ten-year-old Maharaja Duleep Singh, and then passed into British hands.

The Treaty of Lahore, the first peace treaty of the Anglo-Sikh War, stipulated that the Koh-i-noor diamond be given to Queen Victoria.

Similarly, the Cullinan diamond, also known as the Great Star of Africa, was discovered in Africa in 1905. The 3,106-carat Cullinan diamond was cut into nine large diamonds and ninety-six smaller diamonds, many of which are now in British hands.

The Great Star of Africa is set in the Queen's south wing, while the diamond known as Cullinan II is set in the Imperial Crown. The crown was made for Queen Elizabeth's father, King George VI, in 1937, and is based on the design made for Queen Victoria in 1837.

The Imperial Crown, which contains 2,868 diamonds, 17 sapphires, 11 emeralds, 269 pearls and 4 rubies, was worn by Queen Elizabeth until her death in 2017 at the State Opening of Parliament, when the crown became too heavy for the 90-year-old Queen, and was replaced in 2019 with the George VI Diamond Diadem.

The Burmese royal jewel, the Ruby Crown, was reportedly taken by the British and placed in the Imperial Crown, but no one in Burma has ever claimed it back. The world-famous jeweler died on September 8 at the age of 96.

The sessions were attended by a Myanmar delegation, representatives of the International Monetary Fund, 106 global network members and observer organizations, as well as representatives from the United Nations, the World Bank, INTERPOL and the Egmont Group of Financial Intelligence Units. The statement on Myanmar was issued by FATF Chairman T. Raja Kumar.

2. Myanmar is not a member of the FATF, but is a member of the Asia Pacific Group on Money Laundering (APG), a regional group formed by the FATF.

6. Myanmar will only face enhanced due diligence (EDD) by foreign banks when making money transfers abroad, so the relevant banks will be able to continue to ask the usual questions and request evidence of money transfers. (c) Persons permanently disabled in any limb.

Nawsa Al-Shee, who wants to serve her country and save lives

Locals in Kawkareik, Kayin State, are facing food shortages as trade in goods is cut off, leading to a shortage of food for most villagers in the surrounding areas.

As the military tension in Kawkareik continues, all roads have been cut off and it is no longer possible to buy and sell goods, leaving all local residents who rely on it facing food shortages during the rainy season, traders in southern Kawkareik Township said.

A woman who runs a grocery store said, “The road to Kawkareik is very difficult. The price of goods has also increased. It is not easy to buy. During the rainy season, the other roads are broken. We cannot cross the stream and there is a shortage of food. Some villagers are also having a hard time fleeing the war.”

In addition, the Kawkareik-Myawaddy Asian Trade Road is also closed, which is a problem for all businesses that operate in the two countries. They have to travel through the forest roads to transport their goods, which causes delays and risks on the road, border traders said.

A Myawaddy border trader said, “The people are very distressed because the Asian Road is not accessible. It is also difficult to transport goods. During the rainy season, the roads are completely broken. It is very dangerous to travel. The road is also very slow.”

Currently, the military council has re-entered and controlled Kawkareik town and invited residents to return to their homes, but the villages near the town are still not allowed to return and all roads leading to Kawkareik town have been closed, according to villagers.

Similarly, due to the military tension in the town, local residents who rely on Kawkareik town are facing hardship, while many businessmen and workers who mainly operate on the Thai-Myanmar border trade are also facing difficulties.

The farmers say that golden apple snails are present in the entire farmland in the area, and nearly a hundred acres of land are facing this threat.

"These creatures are destroying many acres of land in this area. It is not decreasing. It is more than a hundred acres of land. The reproduction rate is also faster than that of Myanmar snails, so it is getting worse and worse than in previous years," said a farmer.

In these areas, rivers are abundant and during heavy rains, irrigation, In low-lying areas where water is difficult to drain, golden snails attack rice every year. Once the snails invade, the entire field is often destroyed to the point where no one can save it, said a farmer.

“As soon as a little water enters the field, these golden snails enter and destroy the seedlings. They eat them to the point of death. They are worse than rats. When rats enter, there is little left. These snails eat the entire field until not a single plant remains,” he told KIC.

In 2017, the Ministry of Agriculture, Livestock and Irrigation reported that more than 10,000 acres of rice fields were destroyed by golden snails across the country. The golden snails are not native to the region, but are an invasive species that have been introduced from abroad and have been reducing rice yields and harming the interests of farmers for almost a decade.

Currently, farmers are facing the problem of the snails and are finding it difficult to plant rice. Therefore, the local farmers say that the snails usually reduce the yield of the rainy season rice, so they are mainly planting summer rice.

A rice farmer said, "These insects are very bad. They eat all the seedlings. When they enter, even 4 or 5 acres, within two or three days, not a single plant remains. We have to re-sow the rice. Farmers are suffering until they have to plant new rice."

Local farmers said that due to the snails, it is difficult to re-plant rice on time this year, and some farmers have stopped planting rainy season rice, while some farmers are only planting after planting seedlings in areas where there is no water.

"Golden snails usually only feed in areas with water. And they don't eat mature rice plants. That's why some areas that can be drained have to be dug up to drain the water. Some farmers have to plant the plants first and then replant. Others wait until the winter rice is planted," said a rice farmer.

Golden snails in this condition arrived from Taiwan in 1982 as seafood to the Philippines, and from there, they were transported to countries such as Da Nang Port in Vietnam, and from Vietnam to inland Laos and Thailand. They did not arrive naturally, but were brought in by humans and were first identified as pests in 1986. When the golden snail arrived in Myanmar, it first arrived in the eastern regions, Kachin, Shan, Kayah, Karen, and Mon states, according to records.

UN reports evidence of war crimes committed by Myanmar military

August 14, 2024. KIC 

The United Nations Security Council (UN) Independent Investigative Mechanism on Myanmar (IIMM) announced on August 13 that it has received evidence of serious and atrocious war crimes committed by the Myanmar military during the 2023-2024 period, when the military took power.

The IIMM said this in its annual report, which collects and analyzes evidence of war crimes and crimes against civilians committed by the military council between July 1, 2023 and June 30, 2024, when the armed conflict was escalating across Myanmar.

“We have collected extensive evidence of horrific atrocities and inhumane acts of violence across Myanmar,” said Nicholas Khunjan, head of the IIMM, in the report. 

The evidence obtained by the IIMM shows that the military council has carried out airstrikes on schools, religious buildings, and hospitals, displayed mutilated bodies in public, and mutilated those it has detained during the conflict. 

In addition, the military council has documented torture and other forms of torture, including beatings, electric shocks, and sexual violence against detainees, the annual report states. 

The IIMM has collected photographs, videos, audio recordings, The report was compiled based on documents, eyewitness accounts, and sources, and is currently preparing to prosecute the perpetrators.

The IIMM has also obtained evidence of extrajudicial killings of suspected civilians by the military and the insurgents, and is continuing to investigate crimes committed after 2021, as well as crimes committed against the Rohingya in 2016 and 2017.

The National Unity Government (NUG), which was formed after the coup, has also told local media that it will take effective action against crimes committed by its People’s Defense Forces against the people and crimes committed by its own resistance fighters.

The military escalation across Myanmar has intensified since the launch of Operation 1027 in northern Shan State in 2023, and there have been many civilian deaths in the conflict.

The IIMM was established by the UN in 2018 to gather evidence and prepare cases for prosecutions of international crimes and other violations committed in Myanmar, and to promote justice and accountability.

According to data from the Real Estate Information Center (REIC), Myanmar residents bought 1,050 condos worth 5.46 billion baht in the first nine months of 2024. The previous year, there were only 247 units worth 2.25 billion baht.

Condo sales to Myanmar residents from Thailand were still strong compared to the previous year, mainly because most of the purchases were made at the beginning of the year and had already transferred money abroad. 

Myanmar residents bought 564 condos worth 3.7 billion baht in 2023. This is an increase from 349 units worth 2.55 billion baht in 2022. The total number of units purchased in Thailand in the years before 2022 was less than 50 units worth 253 million baht, a 10-fold increase.

In Thailand, the average price of a condo purchased by Myanmar citizens was 5.2 million baht, while Indian buyers bought condos for 6.3 million baht. The average price of a condo purchased by American buyers was 5.3 million baht.

In addition, Chinese buyers were the largest foreign buyers of Thai condos in the first nine months of 2024, purchasing 4,386 condos worth 20.2 billion baht, accounting for 39.7 percent of the Thai property market. 

In the first nine months of 2024, the total value of condo sales across Thailand was 51.5 billion baht, with 11,036 units, up 3.1 percent from the previous year, but down 1.5 percent compared to the purchase price in 2023.

According to the REIC, the proportion of condos sold to foreigners compared to Thais fell from 13.6 percent to 13.3 percent, but the proportion of value increased from 23.3 percent to 24.2 percent.

In the Thai real estate market, foreigners are the most likely to buy condos in Bangkok, accounting for 38.7 percent. The second most popular buyers are condos in Chonburi, at 36 percent.

Professor Dr. Sai Mon Tha, a prominent figure in the Karen community, passes away 

January 20, 2025. KIC 

Professor Dr. Sai Mon Tha, a prominent figure in the Karen community in politics, peace, tradition, culture and society, passed away on the evening of January 18 in Maryland, United States, according to Mann Than Win Oo, a member of the Karen People’s Party Central Committee. 

At the time of his death, Professor Dr. Sai Mon Tha, a neurosurgeon, was serving as a member of the Karen People’s Party (KPP) and was also the director of the Kwekabaw General Hospital in Insein Township. 

“He was the original secretary of our KPP. When the Karen People’s Party was re-formed, it could no longer be a nationwide party, so when it was formed based on the Ayeyarwady region, he was appointed as the chairman. That is why he was one of the founders of the Karen People’s Party,” said Mann Than Win Oo.

He participated in the establishment of the Karen National Democratic Congress Party during the 1990 election, but did not contest the election because he was a civil servant, according to those close to him. 

Then, during the previous military government, the State Peace and Development Council (SPDC), he was a facilitator for the peace talks between the KNU-Karen National Union and the SPDC in 2002-2003, and he was also a close friend of the leaders of the Karen Peace Council (PC). 

In addition, he participated as a member of the expert group at the national conference held from 2004 to 2007 as a professor of medicine. For his participation, the Military Council awarded him the 2024 Social Excellence Award (First Class). 

“He has done a lot for peace, but the peace process, which is very much needed today, has also been weakened. He has also contributed a lot to our literary and cultural sector. I feel like we have lost our right arm,” said Mann Than Win Oo. 

However, there were differences of opinion at the time regarding his efforts to facilitate a meeting between the former NNU Chairman, General Saw Bo Mya, and the SPDC, and his efforts to promote peace for the SPDC. Dr. Simon Tha was one of the founders of the KPP when political parties were allowed to be established in 2010. In addition, he ran for the position of Minister of the Karen Nationalities in the Ayeyarwady Region in the 2010 election. 

Although he won the election according to the initial results, he lost to a member of the Solidarity Party by a small margin due to early voting, according to a member of the KPP Aung Naing at the time. 

In addition, he was a professor and head of the Department of Neurosurgery, the Myanmar representative to the Southeast Asian Neurosurgery Society, and the American Society of Neurology, and was awarded the Medical Leadership Award by the American Society of Neurology. 

Despite being offered high-paying international jobs for his medical excellence, he remained in the country where he was trained until he retired, according to a friend close to his family.

“The doctor always said that as a Karen, he had two responsibilities in Myanmar. He had responsibilities to the country and his fellow citizens, and he also had responsibilities to his own Karen people. As he said, he served in Myanmar until he retired,” said a friend.

Looking back at Dr. Simon’s social work, he served as the leader of the Karen National New Year Celebration Central Committee (Greater Yangon) for 13 years. During this time, he provided medical treatment to areas hit by Cyclone Nargis in 2008 with a mobile team.

Dr. Simon Tha, a prominent figure in Karen Party politics, peace, and a professor in the field of medicine for over 30 years, passed away (fallen asleep in Christ) on January 18 while living in the United States. 

He is survived by his wife, Dr. Naw Rebekah, two daughters, and a son, and his family will hold a funeral in the United States, the KPP said. 

Dr. Simon Tha loved the Karen people very much, but his political stances did not receive widespread support from the Karen people, noted Sayar Saw Kapi, a Karen scholar.

Trump suspends refugee program hours after inauguration

January 21, 2025. KIC 

The White House announced that the United States has temporarily suspended its refugee program hours after Donald Trump took office as president of the United States. 

The White House said in a statement that the United States is temporarily suspending its refugee program because it lacks the financial and resources to help refugees, and that large numbers of refugees are arriving in large cities and are struggling to care for them. 

The statement said that refugee applications will be suspended starting January 27. During the suspension, the White House said that only refugees who are essential to the United States and who are approved by the government will be admitted. 

In addition, the old US refugee admission rules for 2021 will be canceled and the new program will be revised and refugees will be allowed to return when they are ready. 

The US is accepting refugees from all over the world, and the UNHCR has not informed Burmese refugees in Thailand about the suspension, Saw Pwe Say, secretary of the Karen Refugee Committee, told KIC. 

“The UNHCR has not informed us anything. However, one thing I heard is that there is a temporary suspension for people living near the state due to the fire in California. On the 9th of this month, I heard that about 7 families of refugees from Ohn Phin were stopped. I don’t know the details,” he said. 

Currently, the US is the only country accepting refugees on the Thai-Myanmar border. In addition, by 2024, 80 percent of the refugees from the Ban Dong Yang, Tham Mahin and Ohn Phin refugee camps have applied for resettlement in the US. 

Of these, about 400 refugees have left for the United States, while arrangements are still being made to interview and medically examine some of the remaining people, according to the Karen Refugee Committee.

The governments of the five neighboring countries must first exchange information to solve transnational crimes, including the problem of money laundering, said KNU-Karen National Union spokesperson Padoh Toney.

Padoh Toney said this in response to a January 20 statement by the Federal Democratic Forces, including the KNU, on the growing cybercrime crisis in Myanmar.

Therefore, we are calling on the international community, whether through diplomatic relations or through ASEAN and UN agencies, to join hands with the federal forces currently controlling various areas of Myanmar to combat cross-border crimes and human trafficking.

A woman official assisting displaced people in Tanintharyi Township told KIC, “Men are responsible for providing for their families, but now that the fighting is over and daily wage earners are forced to go to work, women are constantly worried about how to support their families, which is causing them psychological distress.”

According to the report, Sagaing Region had the highest number of women deaths in a month, with 21, followed by Shan State and Magway Region, with 9 deaths, the second highest.

BWU compiled the list of women injured and killed from independent news outlets and local sources, and the actual number on the ground is likely to be higher.

According to data released by the Assistance Association for Political Prisoners (AAPP), the military council has detained 4,224 women since the coup attempt until February 28, 2025.

The Burma Women's Union (BWU) was founded in 1995 by women leaders who participated in the 1988 mass movement on the Thai-Burma border with the aim of representing the voices of women from all walks of life. BUW regularly publishes monthly women's news, reviews, and reports on women's labor issues.

EU to provide €33 million in humanitarian aid to Myanmar for six projects

March 7, 2025. KIC 

The European Union (EU) announced on March 3 that it will provide €33 million in humanitarian aid to help people affected by the ongoing conflict in Myanmar.

The EU has allocated €76 million in humanitarian aid to people affected by the crisis in Southeast Asia. Of this, €33 million will go to Myanmar, the EU said.

In addition, €32.3 million (32.3 million) has been allocated to Rohingya refugees in Bangladesh and €3.5 million (3.5 million) has been allocated to civil society organizations in India, Indonesia, Malaysia and Thailand hosting refugees affected by the crisis in Myanmar.

Of the €76 million, €6 million will be allocated to the conflict in Mindanao, the Philippines, and €1.3 million (1.3) million for disaster preparedness in Southeast Asia. 

The €33 million for Myanmar will support six activities: emergency food assistance, shelter and sanitation for displaced people, and emergency health care. 

The EU will also support emergency education services, landmine awareness and disaster preparedness, the statement said. 

The EU's humanitarian assistance will be channelled through partners in the region, including international NGOs and UN agencies. 

The EU has stood firmly by the Rohingya refugees in Bangladesh for the past seven years, and the ongoing conflict in Rakhine State, including in the country, has made it impossible for them to return safely, said EU Commissioner for Crisis Management Hadja Lahbib in a statement.

“Myanmar is facing the world’s worst humanitarian crisis, and the EU has increased its support every year since the 2021 military coup. Our new funding will help vulnerable people in Southeast Asia,” she said.

US President Donald Trump’s decision to suspend USAID’s global aid from January 27 has caused a huge impact on the health and food security of refugees fleeing the conflict along the Thai-Myanmar border, according to groups helping refugees in the Kawthu Lai region. 

Therefore, in order to prevent the refugees from becoming a major problem, we are also continuing to talk to international INGOs about obtaining support from Europe, and there is a good chance of getting help, said Saw Ke Lay, deputy head of the Karen Internally Displaced Persons Committee (CIDKP).

He said, “I have talked to them about getting support from the European Union, and they know this. I have also talked to INGOs/NGOs about the support from the Australian government. I have received a good response. But we have to wait for the support. It is not easy to replenish it like before.”

In addition, a woman from Hpa-an said that she is worried that when local donors and civil society organizations help refugees who have fled their homes due to the conflict, they will be arrested for illegal association.

“There are many people in the villages who are facing difficulties and are fleeing the war. We can’t donate like we used to. When we see donations, PDF groups are supporting them, so we don’t dare to help each other. There is no fundraising for the war. There are many people in our own country who want to help each other. If we donate, we can be charged with supporting PDF, so we don’t dare to donate,” he told KIC.

UN agencies have reported that the number of displaced people in Myanmar has increased from just over 600,000 before the military coup in 2021 to 3.5 million in the three years to 2024, raising humanitarian needs to unprecedented levels.

Thanmani Soe Lin Oo Loses Again on Points Due to Lack of Preparation

March 8, 2025. KIC 

Karen traditional boxer Thanmani Soe Lin Oo lost to Russian fighter Dmitrii Kovtun on points at ONE Championship’s ONE Fight Night 29 on March 8 in Bangkok, Thailand.

He had only about a month to prepare for his fight with the Russian fighter, but he told KIC on March 4 before the fight that he would give it his all. 

Thanmani Soe Lin Oo had only about a month to prepare for the fight, and after a three-round fight today, his opponent Kovtun won on points. 

Including today’s fight, Soe Lin Oo has won three of his six ONE Championship matches, winning three straight by knockout, and losing three of his last two by knockout.

On November 30, 2024, Soe Lin Oo was in a car accident near Kyauk Khet Village, Myawaddy Township, Karen State. After being discharged from the hospital, he fought against Thai fighter Seksan (SEKSAN) in the ONE 170 match on January 24, and now he is fighting again.

Women’s groups warn of continued efforts to bring sexual abusers to justice

March 8, 2025. KIC 

Twenty-five women’s groups, including the Women’s League of Burma (WLB), have issued a statement on International Women’s Day, March 8, calling for the unconditional punishment of anyone who commits sexual exploitation, abuse and violence against women.

The women’s groups said they will continue to monitor the situation to ensure that perpetrators of sexual exploitation, abuse and violence against women are given appropriate punishments under the law and that they are held accountable through the relevant legal channels to ensure that perpetrators do not go unpunished. 

“There are always voices calling for women’s rights, equal rights, and an end to human rights violations and violence against women and impunity. We are taking action. So, we will continue to work on this issue, no matter what difficulties or difficulties, until our goals and aspirations are met,” Navid Bun, the policy director of the Women’s League of Myanmar, told KIC.

Some are abusing their authority, power, authority and trust to commit sexual exploitation, harassment and violence during the conflict, which is particularly damaging to the safety of women who are participating in the revolution based on their faith.

In addition, the women’s groups warned in a joint statement that they should immediately stop targeting and threatening those who speak out against violence and those who support it.

In addition, we urge our organizations to work together, invite speakers, provide space, communicate, and recognize women as social punishments to strengthen the system of accountability and justice for women who have been abused.

In 1857, women workers in the United States demonstrated in New York City against workplace inequality, but were unsuccessful and faced harsh repression. In recognition of this, March 8 has been celebrated as International Women's Day since 1911.

LGBT activist and writer Saw Han Nwe Oo (b.) Naw He Nay Htoo passes away

March 10, 2025. KIC 

Writer Saw Han Nwe Oo (b.) Naw He Nay Htoo, a political activist and well-known LGBT activist in Mae Sot, on the Thai-Myanmar border, passed away yesterday (March 9) evening somewhere in Mae Sot, according to those close to her.

She was suffering from lung disease, malaria and asthma, and passed away at around 9 pm on March 9, according to her close colleagues.

“I know she has been in the hospital for a long time. I am happy to see that she has posted a message on her account saying that she is feeling better. I am saddened by her sudden passing,” a close person told KIC.

The writer, Saw Han Nwe Oo (b. Naw He Nay Htoo), had been receiving medical treatment in Chiang Mai, Thailand since the second week of December 2024, and was transferred to Mae Sot Hospital through Chiang Mai and passed away while receiving medical treatment.

Saw Han Nwe Oo (b. Naw He Nay Htoo) also did some independent work related to the Spring Revolution and often participated in the painting and photography exhibitions of the revolutionary community. She is also known as an LGBT activist in that community and is said to have been open about her identity as an LGBT.

She was born in Hinthada, Ayeyarwady Region, and after graduating, she worked in local civil society organizations (CSOs). After the 2021 military coup, she participated in the protests and received two months of military training with the ethnic resistance group in northern Burma before returning to Mandalay. She was arrested by the military council in September 2021 and released from prison two months later.

She then returned to the liberated areas and worked as an activist. Her real name was Saw Daniel Lin Aung and she was 28 years old at the time of her death. Her funeral will be held at Mae Taw Clinic today, March 10, at 1:00 p.m.

Saw Myint U and his team were attacked by drones while attending the opening ceremony of the new Jaing (Kawkareik) bridge connecting Hpa-an and Kawkareik towns, which was attended by Kayin State Chief Minister Saw Myint U and his team on March 9, and were attacked by drones, causing injuries to soldiers and civilians, the Mon State Liberation Army-MLA said in a statement yesterday.

The Spring UAV Force - G3 Fixed-Wing drone team under the MLA launched three drone attacks at around 5:00 am and 8:00 am on the 9th. As a result, three (3) members of the Military Council were killed, at least five (5) were injured, and one (1) civilian was injured, and Saw Myint U and his team were forced to leave immediately, the statement said.

The Military Council's Infantry Battalion, 545th Infantry Battalion, The statement said that a drone bomb dropped on the opening ceremony site due to the Japanese equipment installed at 546 and Hirthigone injured a civilian vendor near the primary school below the old bridge.

A village administration official who did not want to be named told KIC, “On the day the Japanese bridge was opened, two drones fell on the Jain Kindergarten, killing six children. It was not too bad. They were receiving medicine at Kyondo Hospital, and the other one fell on the Japanese site, but it did not hurt anyone. It was in Jain village. There were about 20 soldiers hiding near the Thayet Taw village school.”

Due to the discrepancy in the statement regarding the civilian casualties, Karen News Agency-KIC contacted the relevant revolutionary forces, including the Mon Army MLA, to obtain confirmation. An MLA information officer responded as follows:

“Only one person was injured. This is very sad. The other casualties were the soldiers on the bridge,” he said.

At the same time, the MLA also advised the public to avoid being close to the military council’s ceremonies and events.

The new bridge, which is part of the East-West Economic Corridor, which connects Myanmar’s Thilawa Port to Thailand, Laos and Vietnam, was built with Japanese technology at a cost of more than 6 billion yen and is nearly 2,000 feet long, according to the Roads and Bridges Department under the military council.

Therefore, the Chief Minister of Karen State under the military council, Saw Myint U, as well as the Ministers of Construction, Transport and Justice, and the Deputy Commander of the South-Eastern Military Command, attended the ribbon-cutting ceremony of the landmark bridge.

Most trucks on the Myawaddy-Pha-An route have been stopped due to numerous arrests, traders face difficulties

March 11, 2025. KIC 

Since March 5, hundreds of trucks carrying Thai goods have been stopped and inspected by the State Military Council at the entrance to Hpa-An town in Kayin State, and most Thai trucks on the Myawaddy-Pha-An route have been temporarily stopped, truck drivers said. 

A trader transporting goods on the Myawaddy-Pha-An route said that the military council is still stopping more trucks and inspecting them, and that there is little traffic on both large and small trucks, and some have stopped running. 

“For now, it’s quiet. Since a lot of big trucks have been stopped in Hpa-an, I don’t dare to go. I’m afraid. They’ve stopped them at both the entrance and exit of Hpa-an, and the number of people who have come has also decreased. All Thai goods are exempt from customs duties, so they have the right to stop them. They stop big trucks and small trucks. Right now, they only stop big trucks, but I don’t know when they’ll stop small trucks,” he told KIC.

Traders said that the stoppage of trucks carrying goods has stopped the entry of many Thai goods, and local Thai goods sellers are worried that prices will rise again.

“If they change the route due to the stoppages, the prices will rise again due to transportation costs. The situation is not good. The price of fuel is high. Now they’ve stopped them again,” said a Hpa-an goods seller.

In addition, online sellers of Thai products are facing difficulties between sellers and buyers due to the fact that the ordered products do not arrive on time, and they are dealing with the issue of delayed delivery from buyers on a daily basis, according to those who work in the business.

“Sellers and buyers are dealing with problems almost every day. Some take advance payment for some products, while others do not. Those who have paid in advance have problems when the products arrive later. When they pay for the products, they have to invest their own money and are now worried about the products not arriving, and some have even had to refund the money,” said a woman from Hpa-an who sells online products. 

Hundreds of trucks carrying Thai products have been seized by the State Military Council police, and they have not been released to date, according to Hpa-an residents. In addition, reports of illegal goods being seized are often published in the Military Council’s mouthpiece newspapers. 

Truck owners are reporting that trucks seized by the military council in Phayao are being kept at the provincial government's Sirikwin and negotiations are underway to pay hundreds of thousands of baht to the customs department to release the trucks. Truck drivers also said that they are checking whether the goods are legal or not.

Malaria drugs shortage in Beit-Dawei district

March 12, 2025. KIC 

KNU-Karen National Union, Beit-Dawei district, is facing a shortage of malaria drugs and medical supplies, District Health Officer Pado Naw Al-Seto told KIC.

The shortage of malaria drugs is a result of the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) cutting off humanitarian assistance at the end of January. Regarding the shortage of malaria drugs and diagnostic medical supplies, District Health Officer Pado Naw Al-Seto said:

“There is a shortage of malaria drugs and diagnostic equipment in Beit-Dawei district. This is because USAID has stopped providing assistance, so malaria drugs have been cut. There are difficulties like that. We have to find other ways,” he told KIC.

In addition, respiratory diseases are common in Beit-Dawei district during the current summer season, and malaria is the second most common disease in the district, after the rainy season, Padoh Naw Al-Seto added.

The Karen Health and Relief Department (KDHW) (Central) usually sends malaria drugs and diagnostic equipment to Beit-Dawei district every three months, and has already sent them until February this year. Padoh Daim Moon Khin, in-charge of the KDHW department, said that they are planning to find a way to deliver them for the next three months.

“We have already sent malaria drugs to Beit-Tawei district until February. We are working to find a way to bring more for the next three months. We are also looking for a route. We are planning to send them together with children’s vaccines,” said Padoh Dae Moon Khin.

Apart from malaria drugs, there is no shortage of drugs for other diseases in Beit-Tawei district, according to the district health department.

Justice for Myanmar calls on three countries to follow Switzerland in imposing sanctions on MOGE

March 12, 2025. KIC 

Justice for Myanmar-JFM on March 11 called on Canada, the UK and Australia to follow Switzerland in imposing sanctions on the Myanmar Oil and Gas Enterprise (MOGE).

The JFM called for Switzerland to impose sanctions on MOGE, which is the largest source of foreign tax revenue for the military council and is funding war crimes against the Burmese people.

“The military regime is using gas revenues to purchase weapons and jet fuel to continue its deliberate airstrikes and bombings against civilians who are committing international crimes,” JFM spokesperson Ma Yadana Maung said in a statement. “We call on Canada, the UK and Australia to follow suit and impose sanctions on MOGE,” he said in a statement. 

In addition, the military council earned more than $841 million in three months of revenue from natural gas and oil exports in 2023, the JFM said in a statement. 

Switzerland’s action closes a loophole for the military council amid EU sanctions, and shows solidarity with the people who have been fighting for democracy in Myanmar for four years since the coup. 

The JFM said it is investigating individuals, businesses and organisations involved in war crimes, JFM is known as a secretive organization that conducts research, documents, and reports to the public.

JFM and other like-minded organizations are also working to prevent the import and sale of aviation fuel and military equipment into Myanmar, including MOGE, and to work together to overthrow the military regime.

The Swiss government’s decision to impose sanctions on MOGE was also revealed in a request submitted by JFM to the Economic and Social Affairs Secretariat (SECO) on March 13, 2024, under the Freedom of Information Act, JFM said in its statement.

Pa-O National Day celebrated for the first time at a national school in the liberated area

March 13, 2025. KIC 

The 76th Pa-O National Day, which falls on March 13, was celebrated for the first time at the Suriya Sandar Pa-O National School in the liberated area on the Thai-Burma border.

The Pa-O National Day ceremony at the school began at 7 a.m. and a high school graduation ceremony was also held to honor the National Day, said the school’s principal, Khun Maung Rai.

“This is the first event. The school has only been established for two (2) academic years. It is to preserve and preserve the cultural traditions of the past. We are working to make it unique and different from the annual events. And it is not just a fun event. We are moving forward with an educational model that focuses on education and allows cultural traditions to take their own course,” he told KIC.

The Suriyasanta High School, a Pa-O national school, was established early last year and is currently taught by eight teachers and 26 students, the school’s headmaster said.

The Pa-O National Day and graduation ceremony held at Suriyasanta School was attended by nearly 100 people, including school officials, teachers, students, and guests.

In addition, the 76th Pa-O National Day ceremony was led by the Pa-O National Federal Council (PNSC) and the Pa-O National Liberation League (PNLO/PNLA) and was held online, with leaders from various revolutionary forces attending and delivering speeches.

“The national duty of the Pa-O people is to join hands with all ethnic groups in the struggle for the end of the military dictatorship and the establishment of a federal union with the right to the emergence of new states,” said PNLO/PNLA General Secretary Colonel Khun Aung Mann at the ceremony.

Today’s Pa-O National Day ceremony is being held in Thamanya Township, Karen State, and also in Bin Hlaing Township, Thaton Township.

Dr. Cynthia Maung says she will work with Thai university that awarded her doctorate in teaching and quality improvement
March 13, 2025. KIC

Dr. Cynthia Maung, founder of Mae Sot’s Mae Daw Clinic, said she will work with Nareasuan University in northern Thailand, where she was awarded an honorary doctorate, on teaching and quality improvement.

Nareasuan University awarded Dr. Cynthia Maung an honorary doctorate at a graduation ceremony on March 11 for her social work in the ASEAN region and her contributions to humanity.

Dr. Cynthia Maung told KIC about the award of her doctorate and the offer to collaborate with the university.

“This is an opportunity for us to further develop our collaboration with Narathiwat University, especially in terms of teaching and quality improvement,” said Dr. Cynthia Maung.

In addition, the honorary doctorate is a recognition of our work in health, education, child rights, health-related human resource development, and border issues in the border region.

“It gives us the strength to work more on the health and security issues that are always a concern for the Myanmar migrant community and the people living on the border, and it also gives us the strength to work more with CSOs, especially on the border. On the other hand, we will have more opportunities to work with these universities because they are more recognized,” added Dr. Cynthia Maung.

Dr. Naw Cynthia Maung, who was awarded an honorary doctorate by a Thai university, is the founder of Mae Sot Clinic, a clinic for migrants in the border region. She is a recipient of numerous awards for her contributions to health, education and humanitarian work, including the Asian Hero Award.

KNLA joint forces capture Pulutu camp, at least 2 junta members killed, 11 flee to Thailand

March 14, 2025. KIC 

The Karen National Liberation Army-KNLA joint forces captured the Pulutu camp of the junta in Paing Kyaw Township, Hpa-an District, near the Thai-Myanmar border, on March 14, killing at least 2 junta members and 11 others fleeing with their weapons to the Thai side, a KNLA source confirmed.

The junta, which has been under attack for nearly a month since last February, was captured at 12:17 a.m. today.

The KNLA joint forces captured the camp, killing two junta members and capturing four others alive. The remaining 11 men, carrying two weapons, crossed the river and escaped into Thailand, confirmed Lt. Col. Saw Plai, the commander of Battalion 22.

“We have finally taken control of the camp. Two soldiers were killed. The most responsible person there was the company commander, Kyaw Phyo Htaik. They fled to the Thai side and four of them were shot dead on the shore. The remaining 11 men, including the company commander, fled to the Thai side with two weapons,” the commander of Battalion 22 told KIC today.

During the attempt to capture the Pulutu camp, which had a total of 23 members, only 17 were left after the KNLA opened fire with sniper fire.

The commander of the 22nd Battalion added that the military council provided air support and heavy weapons during the fighting, but due to the lack of air support at the time of the capture of the camp, they were able to finish the attack quickly and also seized some of the ammunition in the camp.

Similarly, some Thai media outlets reported that the hill of the Pulutu camp was burning, as seen from the Thai side, and that the military council members in the camp were fleeing across the Thaung Rin River.

WFP to suspend food aid to one million people in Myanmar from April

March 14, 2025. KIC 

The United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) announced today (March 14) that it will suspend its current life-saving food aid to one million people in Myanmar from April due to funding constraints.

The suspension of aid will also affect the 100,000 internally displaced people in central Rakhine State and the Rohingya community, the WFP said.

“This suspension of aid could have a devastating impact on communities across the country who rely solely on WFP. We will continue to deliver on our commitments, but it is also important that we receive funding immediately to help those in need,” WFP’s Myanmar Representative Michael Dunford said in a statement.

Myanmar needs $60 million to continue its life-saving assistance to 2025, and without new funding, WFP will be able to help only 35,000 people in the country, including children under five, pregnant and lactating mothers, and people with disabilities.

However, WFP will continue to work to provide emergency assistance to 300,000 people who will need assistance during the peak rainy season, July to September.

The number of people in need of humanitarian assistance has increased from more than 13 million in 2024 to more than 15 million this year, according to WFP. In addition, the country’s ongoing armed conflict has led to a global call for more funding to meet humanitarian needs.

The US President’s decision to suspend all USAID and foreign development assistance, citing the country’s national interests, has led to the suspension of many USAID-supported humanitarian programs and operations in Myanmar.

Humanitarian organizations affected by the conflict, including those supported by Donors, are seeking increased support from Western countries, including Europe, and have reportedly suspended their previous operations while they wait for funding.

Morning Market of Wild Fruits and Vegetables in Mae Silit
Htoo Ka Pao (March 10, 2025)
The morning is cool and spring-like, with the sun shining brightly and the surrounding area is clear and pleasant, and the Dawna Mountains and mountain peaks are scattered here and there.

People of both countries protest against construction of dam on Salween River

March 15, 2025. KIC 

People of both countries living near the Salween River will always oppose construction of large-scale hydropower projects on the Salween River. Locals from both countries, living near the river, held a joint protest near the Salween River in Mutaw Township, KNU, on the occasion of the International Day Against Rivers and Dams on March 14.

The construction of a dam to generate electricity will damage the ecosystem and will require the displacement of all indigenous people living near the Salween River, so they will always oppose it for generations to come, said Naw Samu, a member of the Karen Rivers and Streams Watch.

“The Burmese military regime has been working to make the dam project happen. They have been expanding their territory and expanding their territory. In the past, if you protest here, you would be threatened. Now, since the Burmese military is no longer in this area, you can protest freely. No dams are allowed on the Salween River. We must continue to protest so that it can flow freely,” he told KIC.

The dam project on the Salween River has been opposed for years, and this year, local communities from both countries are protesting together to let the international community and those who want to build the project know, said Naw Samu of the Karen Rivers and Streams Watch.

The protest was held on March 14 at Thu Mwe Hta, where the Salween River and the Thaung Rin River meet. The protest was attended by local communities from 40 villages in the KNU, Mutaw District and 5 villages in Thailand, local KNU leaders and comrades, Environmental activists are joining the protest.

“We are very worried about the dam. The indigenous people of both countries will not accept it. We can only survive well because of the Thanlwin River. If this dam is built, our people will not suffer. We have been protesting for over 20 years and will continue to protest,” said Saw Phat Tin Nu, a Thai national living in Muu, Mae Hong Son District, who participated in the protest.

In addition, since the Thanlwin River is the last river that can flow freely, everyone has a responsibility to protect it and we encourage everyone to continue protesting, said Pi Han, a Thai environmental activist at the anti-dam event.

The Karen River and Stream Monitoring Group has issued a statement calling for a halt to projects that extract resources from rivers without the consent of the people, and for the local people’s environmental conservation practices and practices to be recognized and protected.

The statement also called for consideration of resource management policies that protect communities.

Six dam projects are planned on the Thanlwin River, which flows through Shan, Karenni and Kayin States, including the Hat Gyi Dam in Kayin State, which was announced about a decade ago. However, due to opposition, no news has been released about the status of the project.

KNLA (3) soldiers killed, (6) injured in Pulutu camp battle

March 15, 2025. KIC 

Three KNLA soldiers were killed and (6) injured in a battle in which the Karen National Liberation Army-KNLA joint forces attacked and captured the Pulutu camp of the military council in Paing Kyung Township, Hpa-an District, under the control of the Karen National Union-KNU Brigade (7), the KNU-Central reported today.

Pulutu camp, located in the area of ​​the KNLA Brigade (7), Battalion (22), was attacked by the KNLA, including the Karen National Defense Force-KNDO, and the revolutionary forces, starting last February (25), and was finally captured yesterday (March 14).

In addition to the casualties suffered by the KNLA, 12 members of the Military Council were killed and 11 escaped to the Thai side, according to the KNU Central and Battalion (22).

In addition, the KNU-Central reported that the joint KNLA forces captured the Military Council’s weapons and ammunition after they completely captured the Military Council’s infantry battalion, Point 1248, near the Thaung Rin River on the Thai-Myanmar border.

According to the KNU statement, 3 of the 11 members of the Military Council who escaped to the Thai side carrying two weapons and a grenade were injured, and the border source also said that the Thai authorities have provided humanitarian assistance to these members.

During the nearly month-long battle to capture the camp, the military council's artillery and airstrikes forced locals from the village and surrounding areas to flee to Thailand and other KNU-held areas, in desperate need of shelter and food.

Over 400 IDPs Return to Thailand after Fall of Pulutu Camp

March 16, 2025. KIC 

437 IDPs who fled to Thailand after the fall of the Karen National Union-KNU Brigade (7) military council’s Pulutu camp in Paing Kyaw Township, Hpa-an District, returned to their homes yesterday, March 15, with the help of Thai authorities, Thai media reported.

The joint Karen National Liberation Army-KNLA forces captured Pulutu camp near the Thai-Myanmar border on March 14.

During the battle to capture the camp, the military council used artillery and airstrikes on villages inhabited by civilians in the KNLA Brigade (7) battalion (22) area, forcing the locals to cross the Thaung Rin River into Thailand since February.

Yesterday, Thai authorities, Officials from Tak Province’s Taung Song Yang side have been cooperating, and the Thai side is still monitoring the border security, according to Thai media.

A Karen refugee woman from Kalay Pho Kloi village said, “Thailand has given us everything. Yesterday, we returned half and half. But we are afraid of the plane that will come when we return. There is nothing else, we are afraid of the plane,” she told KIC today.

During the recent days of the battle to capture Pulutu camp, the military council not only carried out airstrikes on the camp and its surroundings, but also attacked the villages where the locals live with airstrikes at least twice, dropping 500-pound bombs, causing damage to homes, according to locals.

As a result, Thai authorities and some Christian organizations are providing assistance to the refugees who have fled to Thailand, and the KNU is also providing assistance to the refugees who have fled to the KNU Brigade 7 area.

BGF transfers over 400 more foreign victims of human trafficking to Thailand

March 17, 2025. KIC 

414 foreign victims of human trafficking who were trafficked to work in online money laundering and smuggling operations in the Thai-Myanmar border, Myawaddy Township, Border Guard Force-BGF controlled area are being transferred to Thailand today (March 17) from the Friendship Bridge No. (2).

400 Indonesian citizens and 14 Sri Lankan citizens are being transported to Mae Sot International Airport by vehicles from the Myawaddy-Mae Sot Bridge No. (2) under the leadership of Lieutenant Colonel Naing Maung Zaw, a member of the BGF’s Special Anti-Human Trafficking/Smuggling Unit.

It was also reported that among the 14 Sri Lankan citizens transferred, 13 were detained by the Democratic Karen Benevolent Army-DKBA.

The BGF’s special anti-trafficking team, which was formed on February 12, has been conducting inspections and clearing up suspected trafficking areas in the Shwe Kuk Kol area since February 14.

As of March 17, 7,523 citizens from 30 countries have been identified as trafficked in trafficking activities, and 3,989 of them have been transferred to their respective countries through Thai authorities, according to a list compiled by the BGF.

Among the foreigners identified by the BGF, nearly 5,000 are Chinese nationals, and six key individuals involved in trafficking have been identified and detained, the BGF said at a press conference held a month after the special team was formed.

The BGF has also made it clear that while the victims of human trafficking are being handed over to Thai authorities through the usual means, the main individuals will be systematically transferred by connecting them with the relevant authorities as the perpetrators.

Japanese national, key figure in online money laundering/human trafficking, to be handed over

March 17, 2025. KIC
